# Introduction

`r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("miREA")` performs microRNA-oriented enrichment analysis
by modeling miRNA-gene interaction (MGI) networks directly, rather than
collapsing them to miRNA- or gene-level sets. Conventional node-centric
enrichment approaches treat miRNAs and genes as independent units, which
discards the inherent many-to-many structure of miRNA-gene regulation and can
bias functional interpretation. miREA instead models the regulatory edges
themselves.

The package implements the following methods.

* **Four node-based methods** are `TG_ORA`, `TG_Score` (target-gene-based),
  `MiR_ORA`, `MiR_Score` (miRNA-based).
* **Five edge-based methods** are `Edge_ORA`, `Edge_Score1D`, `Edge_Score2D`,
  `Edge_Topology`, `Edge_Network`, spanning over-representation,
  scoring-based, topology-aware, and network-propagation approaches.

All nine methods share a common workflow. Prepare method-specific input data
with `getAllInputData()`, run the selected methods with `miREA()`, and
visualize results with `plotSummary()`, `plotHeatmap()`, or
`plotHeatmapSankey()`.

## Relation to existing packages

Several Bioconductor/CRAN packages address related but distinct questions.
`r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("clusterProfiler")` performs over-representation and
gene set enrichment analysis, but for gene enrichment analysis. It tests a 
list of genes against pathway gene sets, with no special focus on miRNAs. 
`r BiocStyle::CRANpkg("CePa")` incorporates pathway topology via node
centrality measures but operates purely on gene-level and node-level, with 
no focus on miRNAs as well.
`r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("multiMiR")` and similar miRNA-target database
packages retrieve curated or predicted miRNA-gene interactions but do not
provide an enrichment/significance-testing framework over them.
`r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("miRNApath")` performs over-representation analysis
by expanding each miRNA-gene pair into its own hypergeometric test unit,
using a single ORA-style method.
`r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("MIRit")` is a comprehensive, actively maintained
framework for integrative miRNA-mRNA analysis, covering differential
expression, correlation-based integration, and gene-set enrichment of
miRNA targets.
Here, we present miREA, to our knowledge the first miRNA-oriented
enrichment package that adopts an MGI (miRNA-gene interaction)
edge-centric enrichment. It spans over-representation, scoring,
topology-aware, and network-propagation methods, and uses
expression-informed edge scores rather than a plain membership test to
characterize miRNA function at the pathway level. Internally, its ORA and
GSEA-style methods (`TG_ORA`, `MiR_ORA`, `Edge_ORA`, `TG_Score`,
`MiR_Score`, `Edge_Score1D`) reuse `r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("clusterProfiler")`'s
`enricher()`/`GSEA()` rather than reimplementing them.

# Installation

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages("BiocManager")
}
BiocManager::install("miREA")
```

# Example data

This vignette uses a small, self-contained example dataset bundled with the
package (see `?miREA_example_data`), derived from the real bladder urothelial
carcinoma (BLCA) data used in the miREA manuscript. The toy_pathway covers 10
Reactome pathways with 1,145 unique genes. toy_gene_DEdata and toy_mir_DEdata
are derived from 422 TCGA samples (403 tumor and 19 normal, used for
differential expression). The 403 tumor samples are also used for miRNA-gene
correlation. The toy_gene_DEdata and toy_gene_mat retain the genes from the
toy_pathway. The toy_mir_DEdata and toy_mir_mat retain 790 miRNAs that target
a toy_pathway gene (via background_MGI) and are DE-testable in the full
manuscript run. The background_GGI_Reactome contains 464,630 gene-gene
interactions (GGIs) from Reactome. The background_MGI contains 306,150 MGIs
from Hua, X., Li, Y., Pentaparthi, S.R., et al. (2023). Landscape of
MicroRNA Regulatory Network Architecture and Functional Rerouting in Cancer.
Cancer Res, 83, 59-73. For the full datasets used in the manuscript, see the
[Zenodo deposit](https://zenodo.org/records/18803209).

```{r load-data}
library(miREA)
data(toy_pathway)
data(toy_gene_DEdata)
data(toy_mir_DEdata)
data(toy_gene_mat)
data(toy_mir_mat)
data(background_MGI)

head(toy_pathway)
dim(toy_gene_mat)
dim(toy_mir_mat)
```

# Step 1: Prepare input data

`getAllInputData()` builds the method-specific input formats (DE gene/miRNA
lists, ranked score vectors, MGI dictionaries, GGI networks, etc.) from the raw
expression and differential-expression tables. Here we request all nine
methods at once. See `?default_method_list` for the full list of supported
method names.

```{r get-input-data}
input_data <- getAllInputData(
    methods = default_method_list,
    pathway = toy_pathway,
    mir_DEdata = toy_mir_DEdata,
    gene_DEdata = toy_gene_DEdata,
    background_MGI = background_MGI,
    GGI_source = "Reactome",
    gene_mat = toy_gene_mat,
    mir_mat = toy_mir_mat,
    scoreFun = "rank"
)
names(input_data)
```

## Supplying background_MGI and background_GGI

`getAllInputData()` takes two background network arguments. `background_MGI` 
provides the miRNA to gene interaction universe used by all methods. 
`background_GGI` provides the gene to gene interaction universe used by 
`Edge_Topology` and `Edge_Network`. Both arguments are optional.

When `background_MGI` is left as `NULL`, `getAllInputData()` falls back to
the bundled `background_MGI` dataset, containing 306,150 miRNA to gene
interactions derived from the literature source cited in
`?miREA_background_data`. A custom `background_MGI` must be supplied either
as a character vector formatted as `[miRNA]:[gene]`, or as a two column
data frame with a miRNA column and a gene column.

When `background_GGI` is left as `NULL`, the source used depends on
`GGI_source`.

* `GGI_source = "Omnipath"`, the default, fetches the full Omnipath
  interaction set at run time. This fetch requires the `OmnipathR` package
  and an internet connection. No license based filtering is applied, even
  though Omnipath aggregates interactions from several underlying
  databases under different licenses, some of which restrict commercial
  use. See the Third party data licensing section of the package README
  for how to supply a license restricted subset through `background_GGI`
  instead. The fetched interactions are limited to *Homo sapiens* through
  the default organism setting of `OmnipathR`, rather than through
  explicit species filtering by miREA.
* `GGI_source = "Reactome"` falls back to the bundled
  `data(background_GGI_Reactome)` snapshot, a frozen Reactome Functional
  Interaction network release licensed under CC0, carrying no usage
  restriction.

A custom `background_GGI` must be supplied as a two column data frame
containing a source gene column and a target gene column.


## Interoperability with standard Bioconductor classes

`gene_mat`/`mir_mat` also accept a
`r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("SummarizedExperiment")`
object in place of a raw matrix/dataframe (the first assay is used), and
`pathway` accepts a `r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("GSEABase")` `GeneSetCollection` in
place of the two-column dataframe. This lets miREA plug directly into
analyses that already represent expression data and gene sets in these
standard classes, instead of requiring a manual conversion step.

```{r interop-demo}
library(SummarizedExperiment)
library(GSEABase)

gene_se <- SummarizedExperiment(assays = list(expr = as.matrix(toy_gene_mat)))
mir_se <- SummarizedExperiment(assays = list(expr = as.matrix(toy_mir_mat)))
pathway_gsc <- GeneSetCollection(Map(
    function(genes, name) GeneSet(genes, setName = name),
    split(toy_pathway$gene, toy_pathway$pathway),
    names(split(toy_pathway$gene, toy_pathway$pathway))
))

input_data_bioc <- getAllInputData(
    methods = "Edge_ORA", pathway = pathway_gsc,
    mir_DEdata = toy_mir_DEdata, gene_DEdata = toy_gene_DEdata,
    background_MGI = background_MGI,
    gene_mat = gene_se, mir_mat = mir_se
)
identical(input_data_bioc$data$Edge_ORA, input_data$data$Edge_ORA)
```

# Step 2: Run enrichment analysis

`miREA()` takes a `background` argument that supplies the gene, miRNA, or
MGI universe each requested method is tested against. `background` has no 
bundled default, and `background = NULL` raises an error.

`background` is a named list holding one entry per analysis target. `TG`
holds the gene background used by `TG_ORA` and `TG_Score`. `MiR` holds the
miRNA background used by `MiR_ORA` and `MiR_Score`. `Edge` holds the miRNA
to gene interaction background used by the `Edge_` methods.

Each entry can be built directly from `input_data`, the object returned by
`getAllInputData()` in Step 1. `input_data$pathway$TG` and
`input_data$pathway$MiR` already hold the gene and miRNA universe restricted
to the supplied pathway set.
`input_data$background_MGI` records whichever `background_MGI` was
actually used in Step 1.

The permutation based methods (`Edge_Score2D`, `Edge_Topology`, and
`Edge_Network`) accept a `seed` argument so their results are reproducible
across runs. We set `seed = 42` below. Leaving `seed` unset draws a fresh
random permutation each run.

```{r run-miREA}
background <- list()
if ("TG" %in% names(input_data$pathway)) {
    background[["TG"]] <- unique(input_data$pathway$TG$gene)
}
if ("MiR" %in% names(input_data$pathway)) {
    background[["MiR"]] <- unique(input_data$pathway$MiR$miRNA)
}
if ("background_MGI" %in% names(input_data)) {
    background[["Edge"]] <- unique(paste0(
        input_data$background_MGI$miRNA, ":", input_data$background_MGI$gene
    ))
}

result <- miREA(
    methods = default_method_list,
    input_data = input_data,
    background = background,
    minSize = NULL,
    maxSize = NULL,
    pvalueType = list(TG = "std", MiR = "std", Edge = "neg"),
    pAdjMethod = "BH",
    pvalueCutoff = 1,
    iter = 20,
    ncores = 1,
    seed = 42
)
result$valid_methods
```

`miREA()` returns a `miREAResult` object, a lightweight S4 container for the
per-method result tables, elapsed times, and call parameters, with `$` access
kept for the four fields above for convenience.

```{r show-result-overview}
result
```

`result$result` is a named list with one data.frame per method. For example,
here is the `TG_ORA` result.

```{r show-result}
head(result$result$TG_ORA)
```

All per-method results can also be flattened into a single dataframe (with a
`method` column) via `as.data.frame()`.

```{r show-result-flat}
head(as.data.frame(result))
```

Each method only reports pathways with pvalue and padj below `pvalueCutoff`.
We use `pvalueCutoff = 1` throughout this vignette so every pathway is
returned. The exception is the ORA methods (`TG_ORA`, `MiR_ORA`, `Edge_ORA`).
These methods only report pathways with at least one overlapping
differentially expressed gene, miRNA, or edge, so some pathways can still be
missing even at `pvalueCutoff = 1` (all 10 of the toy pathways happen to have
at least one such overlap here, so none are dropped in this particular
example. On your own data, check `nrow()` of the ORA results against the
number of input pathways to see whether some pathways are silently excluded).

# Step 3: Visualize results

`plotSummary()` compares results across all requested methods, including
positive enrichment rates, a PCA of per-method pathway rankings, pairwise
overlap between methods, and a p-value density plot.

```{r plot-summary, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 6}
plotSummary(result, penrichCutoff = 0.05)
```

`plotHeatmap()` and `plotHeatmapSankey()` visualize a single edge-based
method's result as a miRNA-by-gene heatmap (optionally combined with a Sankey
diagram showing the miRNA-gene-pathway flow). Only the five edge-based methods
are supported, one at a time. 

```{r plot-heatmap, fig.width = 13, fig.height = 5.5}
plotHeatmap(
    method = "Edge_Score1D", result = result, input_data = input_data,
    penrichCutoff = 0.05, n_pathway = 10, n_mir_heatmap = 10
)
```

```{r plot-sankey, fig.width = 13, fig.height = 10}
plotHeatmapSankey(
    method = "Edge_Score1D", result = result, input_data = input_data,
    penrichCutoff = 0.05, n_pathway = 10, n_mir_heatmap = 10,
    n_mir_sankey = 5
)
```

# Choosing methods for your own data

miREA supports 4 node-based and 5 edge-based methods. You do not always need
to run all nine. Select the method(s) most appropriate for your dataset and
research question. See the method performance comparisons in the miREA
manuscript (`r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("miREA")`'s companion
[bioRxiv preprint](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.02.27.708509)) for guidance.

Please note that `Edge_Topology` in particular can be computationally
expensive. Please check the time cost for methods on different pathways in
the miREA manuscript and consider excluding it or increasing `ncores` for
analyses. `ncores` is the main lever for scaling down wall-clock time.

For the permutation-based methods (`Edge_Score2D`, `Edge_Topology`,
`Edge_Network`), we recommend `iter >= 1000` (default is 1000). This
vignette only uses `iter = 20` to keep build time short on the small toy
dataset, and is not representative of real analyses.
